extra_misconceptions.fact: True soil combines weathered mineral particles with decaying organic humus, water, air, and billions of microbes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Soil is simply crushed rock dust that contains no living organisms or organic matter.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Tiny clay platelets pack tightly with microscopic pores that hold water and slow drainage compared to coarse sand.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pure clay soil drains water faster than sandy soil because clay particles are tiny.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium are the three primary macronutrients required in large amounts by all plants.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium are trace micronutrients needed only by flowering trees.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Chemical fertilizers supply soluble ions, whereas compost, manure, and cover crops restore organic humus and structure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Synthetic chemical fertilizers alone can rebuild depleted soil organic matter and pore structure.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a moist soil sample during a hand ribbon test when clay content exceeds forty percent?
Which physical property distinguishes silt particles from coarse sand and microscopic clay platelets?
What measurement confirms the percentage of sand, silt, and clay after a jar settling test finishes?
Why is it dangerous to mix chemical soil testing reagents without wearing eye protection and gloves?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sheet erosion removes thin, uniform surface layers of topsoil across a slope, while concentrated flow carves rills.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sheet erosion carves deep, narrow trenches across a farm field during a single thunderstorm.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rills are shallow channels removable by normal farm cultivation, whereas gullies are too deep for standard equipment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rill erosion and gully erosion are identical processes that can both be smoothed out by normal tillage.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wind erosion primarily lifts fine silt, clay, and organic topsoil particles from dry, bare fields during steady winds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wind erosion only moves heavy gravel and boulders across desert landscapes during tornadoes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Eroded sediment clogs waterways, smothers fish spawning beds, and reduces water storage volume behind downstream dams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Topsoil washed off farmland stays on the property and increases downstream reservoir storage capacity.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout position a scale ruler when photographing a gully or rill erosion site in the field?
Which physical indicator separates sheet erosion from rill and gully erosion on a sloped hillside?
What depth measurement confirms that a small hillside rill has eroded into a true gully channel?
Why is it dangerous to stand directly on the overhanging lip of an actively eroding gully bank?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Contour plowing follows level elevation lines across a slope so each furrow acts as a small barrier to slow runoff.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Contour plowing means running tractor furrows straight up and down the steepest grade of a hill.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Strip cropping alternates bands of closely sown cover crops with row crops to trap sediment and slow sheet flow.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Strip cropping plants a single cash crop across an entire hillside to maximize harvest speed.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rows of trees and shrubs are planted perpendicular to prevailing winds to block gusts and reduce topsoil blowing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Windbreaks and shelterbelts are planted parallel to prevailing winds to funnel air across bare soil.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Grassed waterways are broad, vegetated channels that slow concentrated runoff and prevent gully formation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Grassed waterways are bare dirt ditches dug to drain storm runoff as fast as possible off a slope.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to surface water runoff velocity when a farmer plows furrows along the contour of a hill?
What structural difference separates broad-base terracing from alternating strip-cropping bands?
Which field measurement confirms that a grassed waterway has the proper parabolic cross-section to prevent gullying?
Why is it dangerous to walk across active agricultural terraces without checking for operating farm machinery?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A watershed is the entire land area that catches rain and snow and drains it into a common stream, lake, or river.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A watershed is a municipal storage building or water tower that holds treated drinking water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Watershed divides follow the highest ridgelines and peaks that split surface runoff between adjacent drainage areas.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Watershed boundary lines on a topographic map run along the lowest valley floors beside creeks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Contour V-shapes crossing a stream valley always point upstream toward higher elevation and the stream source.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Contour lines that form V-shapes where they cross a stream always point downstream toward the mouth.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Small sub-watersheds nest inside larger river basins, carrying upstream runoff and pollutants to downstream communities.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pollution dumped into a headwater creek stays in that small sub-watershed and never reaches the river basin.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout draw the boundary line on a contour map to outline a first-order stream watershed?
Which contour line pattern distinguishes a drainage ridgeline divide from a stream valley on a topographic map?
What elevation measurement confirms whether precipitation falling on a saddle drains into the northern or southern creek?
Under what condition does a field team need a waterproof map case and compass when verifying watershed divides?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Percolation moves water downward by gravity, whereas capillary action draws moisture upward and sideways through pores.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Percolation and capillary action both describe gravity pulling rainwater downward to the water table.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Transpiration is the release of water vapor into the atmosphere through microscopic leaf pores of living plants.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Transpiration is the direct evaporation of rainwater from bare pavement and open lake surfaces.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Removing vegetation eliminates root channels and leaf interception, causing rapid surface runoff and flash flooding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Clear-cutting forest vegetation from a hillside slows down stormwater runoff and increases aquifer recharge.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The underground water table rises during wet recharge periods and drops when drought or heavy pumping removes groundwater.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The water table sits at a fixed depth underground that never changes during droughts or heavy rains.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the water level in a dry soil column when its base is placed in a shallow pan of water?
Which physical force pulls water upward through tiny soil pores during capillary action against gravity?
What measurement confirms the percolation rate when pouring a fixed volume of water through a gravel-and-sand tube?
Why is it dangerous to clamp glass soil demonstration tubes too tightly onto a metal ring stand?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Primary treatment relies on physical screens, grit chambers, and settling tanks to remove floating and heavy solids.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Primary wastewater treatment uses aerobic bacteria and chlorine to sterilize dissolved organic chemicals.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High biochemical oxygen demand means microbes decomposing organic waste are consuming the dissolved oxygen fish need.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A high biochemical oxygen demand reading indicates that a river has abundant oxygen for trout and bass.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Secondary treatment uses aerobic microorganisms in trickling filters or activated sludge tanks to digest organic matter.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Secondary wastewater treatment removes heavy gravel and plastic trash using coarse metal bar screens.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Heated discharge lowers the water's capacity to hold dissolved oxygen and stresses cold-water aquatic species.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Thermal water pollution from power plant cooling discharge improves water quality by warming cold streams.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to suspended solids during primary wastewater treatment before effluent enters aeration tanks?
Which biological mechanism distinguishes secondary waste treatment from primary grit screening and settling?
What measurement confirms that high biochemical oxygen demand is depleting dissolved oxygen in a polluted stream?
Why is it dangerous to collect water samples near a storm outfall without waterproof gloves and hand sanitizer?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Check dams need a lower center notch keyed into the banks so high water flows over the middle instead of cutting around.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A gully check dam should be built higher in the center than at the banks to block all water flow.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bare-root seedlings dry out and die within minutes unless kept moist inside a shaded planting bag until placed in soil.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tree seedlings survive best when their roots are left exposed to sunlight and wind before planting.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rotational grazing gives pasture grasses rest periods to rebuild deep root systems that hold soil and absorb rain.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Continuous heavy grazing in a single pasture all season maximizes grass root depth and water infiltration.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most street storm drains flow directly into local creeks and rivers without passing through a wastewater treatment plant.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Washing paintbrushes or draining motor oil into a street storm drain sends the waste to a sewage plant.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a newly planted tree seedling if air pockets remain around the roots after backfilling?
Where should the spillway notch sit on a rock check dam so storm flow stays in the middle of the gully?
Which field metrics should a Scout record during a site visit to support a five-hundred-word conservation report?
Under what condition must a Scout crew pause work when digging planting holes or lifting rocks in a gully?
